verified_disagreement.subject: P3R2-C-05 (A10 rank 2): old06 killed it at P4 gate G7; new06 selected it at rank 3; A10 independently blind-ranked it 2.
verified_disagreement.old06_position: G7 fail at 67.4: qualification gap 'already active', no primary/official 2028-2035 trigger, and 'a credible path for OCP or vendor labs to standardize it before a 2030 launch'.
verified_disagreement.new06_position: Rank 3 on the factual predicate that Google published its Project Deschutes 2MW CDU specification (3C approach temperature difference, ~80 PSI) via OCP with eight named vendors building to it, while OCP cooling standardization 'remains partial — draft coolant guidelines, a quick-disconnect spec still in revision, and no complete conformance test method with reference hardware' (sources/new06/outputs/50_deep/DEEP/D03.md).

verification.claim: Google contributed the fifth-generation Project Deschutes CDU specification to OCP and published the specification and design collateral.
verification.evidence: Google Cloud Blog post dated 2025-10-13 (opened in full): 'we announced Project Deschutes, a state-of-the-art liquid cooling solution that we contributed to the Open Compute community, and have since published the specification and design collateral', linking to opencompute.org spec document 'ocp-specification-deschutes-final-2025-09-05'.

verification.claim: A multi-vendor ecosystem builds/demonstrates Deschutes-compliant CDUs.
verification.result: VERIFIED for 7 vendors; the 8th (Stulz) only at trade/search level
verification.evidence: Google's own blog names Boyd, CoolerMaster, Delta, Envicool, Nidec, nVent, Vertiv showcasing demos at OCP Global Summit and SuperComputing 2025. Nidec's official release (opened) confirms a compliant prototype at 2MW-class, 80 PSI, IEEE-519 ULHD VFD, exhibited at SC25. Stulz appears in the DCD headline and search summaries only; the DCD page returned HTTP 403 to fetch.

verification.claim: OCP's cooling standardization is guideline/white-paper class with no complete conformance/qualification program with reference hardware.
verification.result: PARTIALLY_VERIFIED (direction supported; negative claim not fully confirmable)
verification.evidence: Search-level listing of opencompute.org documents shows guideline/requirements/white-paper titles (Cold Plate Development and Qualification white paper; Guidelines for water-based fluids; TCS row-manifold pre-commission guidelines; ACS Cold Plate Requirements; an 'L2L CDU Test Methodology performance rating' white paper). No OCP conformance/certification program with reference hardware surfaced. However, opencompute.org returned HTTP 403 to every direct fetch (blog, wiki, spec PDF), so the OCP pages themselves could not be opened; the existence of a CDU test-methodology WHITE PAPER means the vacuum claim must be read narrowly as 'no certification program with reference hardware', which matches D03.md's own wording but was not confirmed by opening OCP pages.

verified_disagreement.adjudication: New06's factual predicate is substantively correct on opened primary evidence: a buyer-authored, OCP-published 2MW CDU specification with a real multi-vendor implementation ecosystem existed by late 2025, and no OCP conformance program was found. Old06's kill relied partly on a forecast (OCP/vendor labs standardizing the qualification layer before 2030) that had not materialized at the new06 refresh and partly on a strict gate-construction (dated official 2028-2035 trigger) that is methodological rather than factual. A10's independent blind rank 2 aligns directionally with new06. Whether C-05 belongs at rank 2-3 versus merely 'selected' remains a judgment call not settled by these facts.
verified_disagreement.confidence: HIGH on the Deschutes ecosystem facts (two independent primary/official sources opened); MODERATE on the OCP-vacuum negative claim (discovery-level only, OCP fetch-blocked); MODERATE on the overall adjudication that the kill was wrong, because the G7 gate difference is partly methodological.
